topics.label: Introduction to the Hallmarks of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture's learning objectives and reviews the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks in tumor progression.

topics.label: Growth Signaling Autonomy and Proliferative Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream signaling cascades drive sustained proliferative signaling.

topics.label: Differentiation Blocks in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how oncogenic mutations prevent proliferating cells from reaching terminal differentiation in both hematological and solid tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how alterations in the p53 and Bcl-2 family pathways allow cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how normal cells enforce replicative limits through telomeres and senescence, and how cancer cells bypass these barriers to achieve unlimited division.

topics.label: Deregulation of Cellular Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire their metabolic networks to support growth through aerobic glycolysis and onco-metabolite generation.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the requirement, timing, and molecular balance of new blood vessel formation that supports tumor expansion.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Dissemination of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how tumor cells navigate the metastatic cascade to disseminate and colonize distant organs.

topics.label: Conclusion and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation by summarizing the integration of cancer hallmarks and providing closing remarks.
